label: copy-phase input h fed back as the 3rd-5th copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the input token is h (99.5% of activation mass). That is the model reading back its own copied h, at an in_first=0 step. It is limited to early-middle copy positions: input is original token 2-4 (recall_idx 3-5), and it is mostly silent on the final output step. Magnitude is largest when h is original token 2 (recall_idx 3) in long sequences (L=8-9), where top activations reach about 3.0. It is weaker at later positions and in shorter sequences. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on h copied at positions 0-1 or 6+. Some of the misses are weak activations on h outside the window. Some of the false positives are h at the window edge in short sequences.

issues: Minor overclaim: the explanation says the feature 'never' fires on h at copy positions 6+. On the dev split, h at recall_idx 6 fires at a 6-9% rate for L=8-9, at recall_idx 8 (L=9) about 10%, and at recall_idx 2 (L=9) about 3%. All of these carry under 0.2% of activation mass each, so this is noise rather than a systematic class.

The window edge recall_idx 5 is soft. Precision there is only about 0.42-0.56 for L=7-9 and 0.09 for L=6. It does not split cleanly by in_count (0.50 vs 0.55) or by whether the previous token was a digit or a letter (0.66 vs 0.49), so it looks like graded magnitude falling off near threshold, not a missing condition.

Grid check (dev) of precision for in_tok==h by recall_idx and L confirms the structure. recall_idx 3: 0.61 at L=5, rising to 1.0 at L=8-9. recall_idx 4: 0.70 at L=6, about 0.99 at L=8-9. to_go==0 cells are nearly silent (0.02-0.09). recall_idx 1-2 are about 0. Mass is largest at recall_idx 3 with L=9 (19%), which supports the magnitude claim.

Test misses are 1.6% of mass: scattered weak non-h tokens and weak h outside the window. Test false positives are, as the explanation states, h in short sequences (L=5-6) or at recall_idx 5. Alternatives scored worse on test: dropping to_go>=1 gave F1 0.772, and restricting to recall_idx 3-4 gave F1 0.838 (0.768 without to_go>=1). Adding L>=5 changed nothing. The original predicate is about optimal among simple variants.

Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.805, R 0.925, F1 0.861, mass recall 0.984. in_tok==h holds 99.5% of the mass. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and in_first is 0 for every activation.
